questions.question: What is the core evidence invariant for an extracted field?
options: Keep the value linked to its source, schema version, and decision state
Keep only the normalized value after validation
Use the same confidence threshold for every field
Delete intermediate versions after each retry
questions.explanation: Source evidence, contract version, and decision history make a field inspectable, replayable, and safe to correct.

questions.question: A PDF has valid native text on most pages but two scanned signature pages. What is the best first routing decision?
options: OCR every page to keep one processing method
Use native extraction where coverage is trustworthy and OCR the scanned pages or regions
Ignore the signature pages because they are images
Convert the entire PDF to plain text before preserving coordinates
questions.explanation: Page- or region-level routing preserves reliable native evidence while limiting OCR cost and recognition error.

questions.question: Why is correct OCR text insufficient for a two-column report?
options: OCR cannot return confidence
The parser must still infer block roles, reading order, and relationships
Columns are always stored as tables
Correct characters guarantee semantic order
questions.explanation: Character recognition and document structure are different tasks; coordinates alone do not guarantee the intended reading sequence.

questions.question: An invoice total has 0.98 model confidence but does not equal subtotal plus tax. What should a production policy do?
options: Accept it because confidence exceeds 0.95
Average the three monetary fields
Apply the cross-field gate and route or block the candidate according to action risk
Remove the reconciliation rule for scanned documents
questions.explanation: Confidence does not override a declared business invariant; validation and action risk determine the safe route.

questions.question: The parser pool can process 900 pages per minute and receives 720 pages per minute. What is parser utilization?
questions.explanation: Utilization is arrival work divided by service capacity: 720 / 900 = 0.8, or 80%.

questions.question: Why must reviewer capacity be modeled with parser capacity?
options: Reviewers make OCR run faster
A faster parser or stricter routing policy can move the bottleneck into the review queue
Human review removes the need for labeled evaluation
Review queues cannot accumulate backlog
questions.explanation: Parsing and review are coupled service stages; increasing one stage's throughput can overload the next.

questions.question: Which evaluation result most clearly exposes a hidden production risk?
options: A strong traffic-weighted average with a high false-accept rate on scanned financial tables
Equal precision on every document slice
Stable queue age during the burst test
A lower correction rate after reviewer training
questions.explanation: Large easy slices can dominate an aggregate while a small, high-consequence slice fails, so release gates must inspect slice metrics.

questions.question: What makes a parser release operationally reversible?
options: Deploying the new model to all tenants at once
Keeping only aggregate dashboards
Immutable inputs and versions, bounded canary authority, explicit rollback triggers, and a replay procedure
Changing the schema and parser in one unversioned update
questions.explanation: Reversibility requires identifying affected records, stopping authority, restoring a known version, and replaying the same source evidence.
